keywords: how to undo commit in git
title: How to Undo the Last Git Commit (Keeping Changes)
answer: To undo your last Git commit while keeping all your code changes in the staging area / working directory, run: `git reset --soft HEAD~1`.
highlights: Keep Changes Staged: `git reset --soft HEAD~1` (Safest, preserves all edits)
Keep Changes Unstaged: `git reset HEAD~1` (or `git reset --mixed HEAD~1`)
Discard All Changes Completely: `git reset --hard HEAD~1` (⚠️ Destructive)
Already Pushed to Remote: `git revert HEAD` (Creates a safe inverse commit)

title: HTTP Status Code Reference (1xx, 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx)
answer: HTTP status codes indicate whether a specific HTTP request has been successfully completed. Grouped into 5 classes: 1xx (Informational), 2xx (Success), 3xx (Redirection), 4xx (Client Errors), and 5xx (Server Errors).
highlights: 301 Moved Permanently: URL has permanently changed
400 Bad Request / 401 Unauthorized / 403 Forbidden / 404 Not Found
500 Internal Server Error / 502 Bad Gateway / 503 Service Unavailable / 504 Gateway Timeout

title: Difference Between var, let, and const in JavaScript
answer: `var` is function-scoped and hoisted with `undefined`. `let` and `const` are block-scoped and live in a Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ) before declaration. `const` prevents re-assignment of the variable identifier.
highlights: `var`: Function-scoped, can be redeclared & updated, hoisted with `undefined`
`let`: Block-scoped `{ ... }`, cannot be redeclared in same scope, can be updated
`const`: Block-scoped, cannot be redeclared or re-assigned (objects/arrays remain mutable internally)
Best Practice: Use `const` by default; use `let` only when reassignment is needed; avoid `var`
